subject: Different text  annotations within facet_grid on the y-axis

messages.author: 3015c1527bcf288d
messages.subject: Different text  annotations within facet_grid on the y-axis
parts:
Hi,

I have a chart with some lineplot's in one via facet_grid(variable ~ ., ,scales = 'free_y') generated by a melt.
On the y-axis I have now the value string only  and the different scales. 
Now I'd like to do add a  '%' or '€' etc.  to define the unit and for clarifification.

I'm experimenting with geom_text but can't see the text or I got Error: Invalid input: time_trans works with objects of class POSIXct only

What might be my mistake.

Thanks for help
Christian

messages.author: 3015c1527bcf288d
messages.subject: Re: Different text  annotations within facet_grid on the y-axis
parts:
Here is a simple example code to clarify my issue.

library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

df <- data.frame(conversion=runif(100),revenue=runif(100))
df$conversion <- df$conversion * 100
df$revenue <- df$revenue * 1000
df$day <- as.POSIXct(seq(as.Date("2000-01-01"), by = "day", length.out =100))
dfm <- melt(df,measure.vars = c('conversion','revenue'))

ggplot(dfm,aes(x=day,y=value,group=variable,colour=variable)) + 
  geom_point(size=1)  + geom_line(size=1.3) + 
  facet_grid(variable ~ . ,scales = 'free_y') + xlab('Date') + 
  scale_x_datetime(breaks = date_breaks("10 days"), labels = date_format("%d-%b")) 

Now I'd like to have a "%" on the upper line chart  and a '€'  on the lower chart i.e. in the middle of  the y-axis part.

Thanks,
Christian

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Different text annotations within facet_grid on the y-axis
parts:
Hi:

The percentage part is easy; adding the Euro sign means that you need
to include a plotmath character (see ?plotmath for details,
particularly the 'Other symbols' section. You need to create either a
list or vector of expressions, then create a simple labeller function
for facet_grid, then create the ggplot.

I didn't get the Euro symbol when I plotted this, but I don't use
Unicode much so probably missed some detail. However, the process
below is appropriate. I used this symbol table as a reference, where
the Euro sign was listed as symbol 240 in octal:
https://www.stat.auckland.ac.nz/~paul/R/CM/AdobeSym.html

# Create a list of key-value pairs for the labels -
lbls <- list('conversion' = "conversion %",
'revenue' = expression("revenue ("*symbol("\240")*")"))

# Create a labeller function
my_label <- function(variable, value) lbls[value]

# facet_grid() supports labeller functions, so we use it:
ggplot(dfm,aes(x=day, y=value, colour=variable)) +
geom_point(size=1) + geom_line(size=1.3) +
facet_grid(variable ~ . ,scales = 'free_y', labeller = my_label) +

xlab('Date') +
scale_x_datetime(breaks = date_breaks("10 days"),
labels = date_format("%d-%b"))

As I said, on my machine I got a symbol different from the Euro; YMMV.
Perhaps our European friends can edit this to get it right.

Reference: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/19282897/how-to-add-expressions-to-labels-in-facet-wrap,
in the originally posted question.

Note: If necessary, this can be extended to the legend, where you'd
use lbls as the labels argument in scale_colour_manual().

Dennis
